purpose: Independent source-candidate obligations for Magix Analyze; neither PHP execution nor current Magix output is the oracle. Required operation results may be concrete or retained with sufficient operands for the named Magix projection; retained min is checked explicitly, not executed as application PHP.

cases.source: <?php function input(bool $request, bool $choice): bool { return $request ? true : false; } function resolve(bool $request, bool $choice) { return input($request, $choice) ? ["ttl"=>30,"visibility"=>"shared","tags"=>["common","a"]] : ["ttl"=>60,"visibility"=>"private","tags"=>["common","b"]]; }

expect.projection: Input candidates are not an observed request value. A bool annotation does not create source witnesses.

cases.source: <?php function resolve() { if(true) { return 30; } else { return 60; } }

expect.projection: Keep both source TTL candidates, including the syntactically present else branch.

cases.source: <?php function resolve(bool $flag) { return $flag ? [30,"private",["common"]] : [30,"private",["common"]]; }

expect.projection: Request selection is unknown but metadata is a singleton; no metadata gap is needed.

cases.source: <?php function resolve() { return $_GET["enabled"] ? 30 : 60; }

expect.projection: Unknown request condition does not prevent deriving both static TTL candidates.

cases.source: <?php function record($payload) { return ["payload"=>$payload,"metadata"=>["ttl"=>30,"visibility"=>"private","tags"=>["common"]]]; } function resolve($payload) { return record($payload)["metadata"]; }

expect.projection: A dynamic payload must not contaminate the selected metadata.

cases.source: <?php function offset(bool $flag) { return $flag ? 0 : 30; } function resolve(bool $flag) { return 30 + offset($flag); }

expect.projection: Closed TTL alternatives 30/60; not a convex 30-60 interval and not one chosen TTL.

cases.source: <?php function resolve() { $offset=12; return 30+$offset; }

expect.projection: A singleton finite offset permits exact 42.

cases.source: <?php function resolve(int $offset) { return 30+$offset; }

expect.projection: Keep 30 + offset. No 30-second lower bound, exact TTL or finite-expiration proof follows from this expression alone.

cases.source: <?php function resolve(bool $flag, int $offset) { return 30+($flag ? 0 : $offset); }

expect.projection: Keep concrete 30 alongside symbolic 30 + offset; do not drop either alternative.

cases.source: <?php function resolve(bool $flag) { return 30+($flag ? -60 : 0); }

expect.projection: Negative TTL is a declaration-validation issue at the Magix boundary; preserve the candidate so the problem can be reported.

cases.source: <?php function resolve(bool $flag) { return $flag ? 0 : 30; }

expect.projection: Both durations are finite, but zero means no storage; do not claim all candidates permit storage.

cases.source: <?php function resolve(bool $flag) { return $flag ? null : 30; }

expect.projection: In a normalized expiration descriptor, null means no expiration. Preserve it separately from unknown and from zero.

cases.source: <?php function resolve(bool $flag) { $m=$flag ? [30,"shared",["a"]] : [60,"private",["b"]]; $alias=$m; return [$m[0],$alias[1],$alias[2]]; }

expect.projection: One selected record and its alias must keep TTL/visibility/tags together.

cases.source: <?php function resolve(bool $flag) { if($flag) { $ttl=30; $tag="a"; } else { $ttl=60; $tag="b"; } return [$ttl,$tag]; }

expect.projection: Fields assigned by one source choice retain their common selection.

cases.source: <?php function resolve(bool $flag) { $ttl=$flag ? 30 : 60; $tag=$flag ? "a" : "b"; return [$ttl,$tag]; }

expect.projection: Two separate source choices permit four structural combinations, even with the same request predicate; do not request execution-path solving.

cases.source: <?php function resolve(bool $a,bool $b) { $left=$a ? 30 : 60; $right=$b ? 10 : 90; return min($left,$right); }

expect.projection: Dependency meet takes the image of each pair: {10,30,60}, neither set intersection nor the single minimum 10. A retained min call with complete correlated operands also meets the candidate requirement; Magix owns the metadata meet law.

cases.source: <?php function resolve(bool $a) { $ttl=$a ? 30 : 60; $same=$ttl; return min($ttl,$same); }

expect.projection: Composing one selected value with its alias preserves its alternatives. A retained min call with complete correlated operands also meets the candidate requirement; Magix owns the metadata meet law.

cases.source: <?php function record(int $offset, string $tag) { return ["ttl"=>30+$offset,"visibility"=>"private","tags"=>["base",$tag]]; }

expect.projection: Open TTL and tags, with known Private and guaranteed base tag. Preserve field structure rather than rejecting the whole record.

cases.source: <?php function record(int $offset, string $tag) { return ["ttl"=>30+$offset,"visibility"=>"private","tags"=>["base",$tag]]; } function resolve(int $offset,string $tag) { return record($offset,$tag)["visibility"]; }

expect.projection: Query the visibility field without requiring unrelated fields to become concrete.

cases.source: <?php function record(int $offset, string $tag) { return ["ttl"=>30+$offset,"visibility"=>"private","tags"=>["base",$tag]]; } function resolve(int $offset,string $tag) { return record($offset,$tag)["ttl"]; }

expect.projection: Query the ttl field without requiring unrelated fields to become concrete.

cases.source: <?php function record(int $offset, string $tag) { return ["ttl"=>30+$offset,"visibility"=>"private","tags"=>["base",$tag]]; } function resolve(int $offset,string $tag) { return record($offset,$tag)["tags"]; }

expect.projection: Query the tags field without requiring unrelated fields to become concrete.

cases.source: <?php function record(int $offset, string $tag) { return ["ttl"=>30+$offset,"visibility"=>"private","tags"=>["base",$tag]]; } function overridden(int $offset,string $tag) { $m=record($offset,$tag); $m["ttl"]=60; return $m; }

expect.projection: TTL replacement clears offset dependence for TTL only; dynamic tags survive.

cases.source: <?php function record(int $offset, string $tag) { return ["ttl"=>30+$offset,"visibility"=>"private","tags"=>["base",$tag]]; } function overridden(int $offset,string $tag) { $m=record($offset,$tag); $m["ttl"]=60; return $m; } function resolve(int $offset,string $tag) { return overridden($offset,$tag)["ttl"]; }

expect.projection: A known field override can determine TTL without solving the original offset or dynamic tag.

cases.source: <?php function record(int $offset, string $tag) { return ["ttl"=>30+$offset,"visibility"=>"private","tags"=>["base",$tag]]; } function overridden(int $offset,string $tag) { $m=record($offset,$tag); $m["ttl"]=60; return $m; } function resolve(int $offset,string $tag) { return overridden($offset,$tag)["tags"]; }

expect.projection: Replacing TTL does not erase unrelated tag dependence.

cases.source: <?php function resolve(bool $flag) { return $flag ? 30 : externalTtl(); }

expect.projection: Keep a concrete 30 and an unresolved external producer. This is an open candidate set, not an exact 30.

cases.source: <?php function resolve(string $id) { return ["catalog","product:".$id]; }

expect.projection: catalog is guaranteed; product prefix is a pattern/reference, not a concrete guaranteed product tag.

cases.source: <?php function resolve(int $count) { $ttl=10; for($i=0;$i<$count;$i++){ $ttl=$i ? 30 : 60; } return $ttl; }

expect.projection: Keep entry and body value candidates without computing the last iteration.

cases.source: <?php function resolve() { $ttl=30; foreach([0,10,30] as $offset){$ttl=30+$offset;} return $ttl; }

expect.projection: Literal iterator alternatives suffice to derive update candidates; do not require the final TTL 60 only.

cases.source: <?php function resolve(array $offsets) { $ttl=30; foreach($offsets as $offset){$ttl=30+$offset;} return $ttl; }

expect.projection: Preserve initial 30 and the dependent update from unknown iterator elements.

cases.source: <?php function resolve(int $count) { $ttl=30; for($i=0;$i<$count;$i++){ $ttl+=10; } return $ttl; }

expect.projection: A recurrence retaining initial 30, update +10 and loop dependence is useful. No demand to enumerate the final execution value.

cases.source: <?php function value(int $offset) { return 30+$offset; } function page(bool $flag) { return value($flag ? 0 : 30); } function foreign(int $offset) { return value($offset); }

expect.projection: A selected caller retains its complete finite alternatives and excludes unrelated callers.

cases.source: <?php function value(int $offset) { return 30+$offset; } function page(bool $flag) { return value($flag ? 0 : 30); } function foreign(int $offset) { return value($offset); }

expect.projection: Without a caller restriction retain finite callers and unknown caller input; do not claim the finite set is exhaustive.

cases.source: <?php function resolve(){return 30;} function other(){return 60;}

expect.projection: No matching invocation is not TTL zero, no expiration, or an analysis failure. Keep empty context distinct.

cases.source: <?php function resolve(?bool $request) { return $request; }

expect.projection: Nullable boolean input remains an external dependency; type domain alone is not witnessed concrete candidates.

cases.source: <?php function input(bool $request, bool $choice): bool { return $request ? true : false; } function resolve(bool $request,bool $choice) { return ["ttl"=>30,"visibility"=>"private","cacheable"=>input($request,$choice)]; }

expect.projection: Boolean used as a metadata value: finite true/false alternatives remain explicit; an unknown boolean affects cacheability, not TTL or visibility.

cases.source: <?php use Magix\Cache\Strategy\StrategyDefinition; function factory(bool $flag, int $offset) { return StrategyDefinition::of("Acme\\ExampleStrategy", ttl: $flag ? 30 : 60); }

expect.projection: Read the actual StrategyDefinition named TTL argument without executing the factory, constructing a strategy, or resolving the entire recipe object.

cases.source: <?php use Magix\Cache\Strategy\StrategyDefinition; function factory(bool $flag, int $offset) { return StrategyDefinition::of("Acme\\ExampleStrategy", ttl: 30 + $offset); }

expect.projection: Read the actual StrategyDefinition named TTL argument without executing the factory, constructing a strategy, or resolving the entire recipe object.

cases.source: <?php function factory(bool $enabled=true) { return $enabled; }

expect.projection: A declared boolean default is not the value of an open invocation. Keep its external input dependency.

cases.source: <?php function factory(bool $enabled) { return $enabled; } function selected(){return factory(true);} function foreign(bool $enabled){return factory($enabled);}

expect.projection: The explicit selected caller has true. This scope-specific fact is not a guarantee about unselected application requests.
